mcp_api_design_ideas: Model the MCP surface on the Qiskit MCP servers split. IBM lists separate servers for circuit creation and transpile, a transpiler server, runtime, docs, and a community RL server, and recommends testing with npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector (https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/docs/guides/qiskit-mcp-servers). For CQ-HECS this suggests keeping read-only tools (plan, simulate, verify) in one server and any hardware-submission tools in a separate, disabled-by-default server. This also supports the fail-closed hardware rule.

Community quantum MCP servers exist, for example a Qiskit-based simulator with noise models and OpenQASM 2.0 (https://mcpservers.org/servers/YuChenSSR/quantum-simulator-mcp) and an unofficial Qiskit server (https://github.com/barvhaim/qiskit-mcp-server). I saw only their listings and snippets. CQ-HECS's differentiator would be a typed result contract: plan, engine, error scope, refusal reason, run digest.

Add a plan-only tool (dry-run) that returns the ExecutionPlan JSON with candidate paths and rejection reasons, so an agent can ask 'what would you run and why' before spending compute. execution_plan.py and mcp_server.py already exist, so this is mainly a contract and test task.

Expose MCP resources for capability cards and the supported-gate manifest (read-only), so agents can check what is supported before submitting a circuit. Refuse unsupported input with a typed code instead of a free-text error.

Use structured results with explicit enums for mode (ideal, noisy_classical, real_hardware), arithmetic (float64, float32, sampled, exact_gf2), and certificate scope (expectation_only, none). Never a single boolean exact flag.
Accept three input forms: OpenQASM 3 subset, a compact Stim-like text for Clifford circuits, and the JSON circuit; always return normalised_circuit_digest so results can be replayed.

Add an oracle-compare tool that runs the same circuit on CQ-HECS and an installed optional comparator (Aer, Stim) and returns the diff with tolerance, only when the comparator is present locally. No network calls.

OMNIWAVE (cqhecs/omniwave/engine.py): multi-front exhaustive cube search with shared short nogoods, exact coverage accounting, DRAT proof log of refuted cubes, SAT only with a verified model, UNSAT only if coverage is complete and the DRAT check accepts, otherwise UNKNOWN (engine.py:637-664). Plus GF(2) XOR view and quadratic encoding (omniwave/gf2.py, field.py:108), boundary separator counting (boundary.py), optional learned branching (learned.py, off by default), optional batched CPU/Vulkan BCP (bcp.py, gpu.py).

Also max_sat (exhaustive, <=20 vars, sat.py:1273), sweep, enumerate_models.

Test coverage exists for each piece: tests/test_sat_*.py, test_drat*.py, test_omniwave*.py, test_unified_solver.py (12 tests), test_fuzz_sat.py, test_lrat_external.py (skipped unless CQ_CAKE_LPR or CQ_LRAT_CHECK is set).
cannot_do: No CDCL (no clause learning, 1-UIP, VSIDS, restarts) in any in-repo engine, and no preprocessing or inprocessing (BVE, subsumption, SBVA, probing). Everything in-repo is DPLL or exhaustive cube search in pure Python and is much slower than CaDiCaL/Kissat; OMNIWAVE documents itself as slower than CaDiCaL (engine.py header).

No LRAT or other verified-checker pipeline inside the package. LRAT/cake_lpr appears only in an env-var-gated test against a committed pigeonhole_6_5 fixture; the DRAT checker states that it is not formally verified (drat.py:19). research/v7/BLOCKERS.md B-002 records that python-sat, drat-trim, lrat-check and cake_lpr are not installed, so these tests are NOT RUN.

Python threads under the GIL: OMNIWAVE workers do not add speed (engine.py:46). There is no cube-and-conquer, distributed solving or process parallelism. GPU BCP is measured slower end to end and is not the default.

The separator backend refuses above 4000 constrained variables (sat_separator.py:46), above the table budget (default 500k entries), or above induced width 14 under auto. It has no weighted or projected counting, no d-DNNF or knowledge compilation, and no component caching combined with elimination.

CNF-to-XOR extraction exists only for fully encoded parity patterns (omniwave/field.py xor_view). There is no general extractor with an implication witness, and no CryptoMiniSat or BIRD-style Gauss-Jordan integration with proof output.
No incremental or assumption-based API, no MaxSAT beyond the 20-variable brute force (sat.py:1273), no SAT-competition-style output, and no support for industrial instances in the in-repo engines.
defects_or_risks: The unified portfolio mislabels CaDiCaL UNSAT proof status. unified.py:192 sets proof='DRAT proof checked by cqhecs.drat' whenever result.status==UNSAT. But sat_external.py:91 returns status UNSAT even when the DRAT check was rejected, undecided or disabled (certified=False). A certified-sounding label can then accompany an uncertified UNSAT. The same unconditional label is at unified.py:184 for OMNIWAVE, which is safe only because the engine downgrades to UNKNOWN; the cadical path has no such downgrade.

The default first engine, watched, produces UNSAT without any certificate (unified.py _attempt, certify=False). With the default order and stop_on_decision=True, most UNSAT answers from solve_unified are therefore uncertified. UnifiedResult has no 'certified' field, so a consumer must parse the attempt proof strings. That conflicts with the AGENTS_V6 W5 gate 'every UNSAT certificate replayed'.

Time budgets are not honoured end to end. sat_external.py uses a proof budget of max(10 s, 2x timeout), so a CaDiCaL attempt with a 1 s share can run 10+ s in the DRAT check inside the unified call. solve_unified therefore does not honour its stated total timeout.

DRAT checker complexity: _propagates_to_conflict rebuilds the full clause list on every RUP call (drat.py:112) and then runs a naive scan-to-fixpoint with no watches. RAT scans the whole database for each lemma. Checking is roughly O(lemmas x clauses x passes), so realistic CaDiCaL proofs hit the budget and give valid=None (uncertified). The forward-only design has no backward/core-first optimisation.

OMNIWAVE proof size is proportional to the number of refuted cubes (engine.py:385-410), so proofs are large. Its check_proof=False setting makes a completed search UNKNOWN rather than UNSAT (engine.py:651). That is sound, but it makes the feature unusable for performance work.

The unified solver and its schema do not include #SAT or separator counting, so counting and solving have separate, unconnected result contracts (count_models returns an untyped dict with contract_version 1.2). T6-08 in AGENTS_V6.md ('keep budgets + proof soundness') defines no measurable acceptance criterion.

The in-repo sat_separator planner is O(n^2)-ish min-fill (recomputing _fill for touched vertices). It is capped at 4000 variables, but with dense graphs the planner itself can eat the deadline, which then surfaces as SeparatorBudget -> UNKNOWN.

Certification claims rest on v3.7 evidence only: external proof checkers and python-sat are unavailable in this environment (BLOCKERS.md B-002). The known Windows/py3.14 python-sat abort (0xC0000409) risks crashing the whole pytest process if the optional tests are not isolated.

can_do: Runs circuits fully client-side in a worker: Rust/WASM f64 statevector (web/wasm/src/lib.rs, 421 lines, global state, SIMD/bulk-memory build) with shot sampling, mid-circuit measure/reset, Monte-Carlo noise trajectories (depolarizing p1/p2, xflip, asymmetric readout) in web/src/simulate.ts and exact probabilities/amplitudes/Bloch vectors (exact table n<=22, amplitudes n<=6).

Optional WebGPU f32 path (web/src/gpu.ts): single WGSL kernel for 1-target + control-mask gates, 512-op command batches, error scopes for shader/OOM, then CPU inverse-CDF sampling; for n<=20 the worker cross-checks against the WASM f64 core and returns crossCheckTv (engine.worker.ts runGpu).
Safe-run policy (device.ts): WASM_MAX_QUBITS=27, 90 s runtime cap, RAM-budget limit confirmed by a real allocation probe in the worker; oversized circuits are refused (e2e 'safe limits refuse...').
Provenance run card hcs.run.v2 (provenance.ts) shared with the Python schema, input SHA-256 digest, JSON export; EN/DE/FR i18n; lazy CodeMirror editor; bundle-budget check; Vercel headers.

Tests: 63 node:test cases bundled by tests/run.mjs (circuit_conformance, conformance vs. Python-exported quantum_conformance.json at 1e-12, Qiskit statevector fixtures, core/wasm, provenance, forge) plus Playwright+axe e2e (routes, language switch, Bell run, WebGPU-unavailable fallback, layouts, axe) in the CI job web-emulator (.github/workflows/ci.yml:409).
Also hosts a SAT/#SAT/sweep lab in the same worker (sat.ts, satcert.ts) and a SHA-256 'forge' lab with WASM/WebGPU backends and fallback decisions (web/src/forge/).
cannot_do: WebGPU path refuses mid-circuit measure/reset and any gate noise (main.ts:434 throws run.gpuNoise); it is terminal-measurement, noiseless-gates only, f32, and has no Bloch vectors (bloch: [] in engine.worker.ts).

No shared Python<->WASM<->WebGPU conformance run: the corpus (tests/fixtures/quantum_conformance.json) is only consumed by WASM tests; WebGPU is never exercised in CI (headless chromium lacks it; e2e only tests the unavailable fallback). T6-05/T6-06 are NOT STARTED (research/v7/TASKS.md M8).

Cancel is worker.terminate() (main.ts:476), so no partial results, no cooperative stop, and GpuEngine.run is called with shouldStop=()=>false (engine.worker.ts), so the GPU cancellation hook is dead code.

Run card carries no error scope: error.{approximation,numerical,sampling} are all hard-coded null (provenance.ts) even though noise runs are Monte-Carlo estimates and WebGPU is f32; no confidence intervals on counts.

Not the Python four-path engine: no stabilizer/MPS/sparse-Pauli, no Path D observables, no ExecutionPlan, no QG Lab (T6-02 not done); statevector only, hard ceiling n<=27 qubits (2 GiB wasm32), GPU limited by maxStorageBufferBindingSize.
Gate set is limited to what circuit.ts compiles to 1-target + control-mask unitaries; the GPU kernel cannot do multi-target gates natively (SWAP etc. must be decomposed by the compiler).
defects_or_risks: provenance.ts modeOf() only checks p1/p2/readout, while simulate.ts/main.ts also treat xflip and per-qubit p01/p10 as noise: a run with only xflip or only p01/p10 is labelled SAMPLED instead of NOISY_CLASSICAL in the exported card (provenance.ts modeOf vs main.ts:433 gateNoisy).

WebGPU device loss is never handled: no device.lost listener or uncapturederror handler in gpu.ts; a lost device leaves the engine object stale and later runs fail with generic errors (T6-06 requirement unmet).

gpu.ts run() leaks buffers if exceptions happen before the try (state/params created before try block is fine, but the 'read' buffer is not destroyed on mapAsync failure) and allocates one bind group per op (BATCH=512) -- avoidable overhead; PARAM_STRIDE hard-coded 256 ignores requested minUniformBufferOffsetAlignment.

engine.worker.ts fetches '/cqhecs_core.wasm' via new URL(..., self.location.origin): breaks any sub-path/CDN deployment and offers no integrity check; WASM core uses global mutable STATE with unsafe static (lib.rs:20), so concurrent use is unsound if ever shared.

GPU result sampling happens in f64 on the CPU from f32 probabilities with probs filtered >1e-9 and norm taken from f32 sum; for n>20 there is no cross-check, so f32 drift is unreported exactly where it grows (crossCheckTv only n<=20).

trajectoryCount() uses fewer independent trajectories than shots (min 256) for terminal noisy runs, so counts are not i.i.d. shots; the card reports trajectories but no uncertainty (simulate.ts trajectoryCount, AGENTS.md section 3.7 audit item).

Rate benchmark at init (18-qubit H loop, engine.worker.ts benchmark) drives runtime estimates and device labels from a microbenchmark that AGENTS.md section 3.7 warns against; ramGiB from deviceMemory is capped at 8 and Chromium-only.

Committed tests/*.test.bundle.mjs build artifacts sit in tests/ (generated by run.mjs); risk of stale or committed generated files; CI rebuilds wasm but only logs hash difference, never fails on drift.

cannot_do: MCP server speaks only protocol 2024-11-05, hard-coded (mcp_server.py:21); it ignores the client's requested protocolVersion (no negotiation), advertises only `tools` capability, and has no resources, prompts, logging, progress, cancellation handling (notifications/cancelled is dropped at line 400), elicitation, tasks or pagination.

No tool annotations (readOnlyHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint), no `title`, no `outputSchema`/`structuredContent`: results are `json.dumps(indent=2)` text blocks (mcp_server.py:172-173), so clients cannot validate or machine-read outputs. A grep for outputSchema, annotations, structuredContent and isError in cqhecs finds nothing.

Tool failures are returned as JSON-RPC protocol errors with generic code -32000 (mcp_server.py:412-413) instead of `isError: true` tool results, so an LLM cannot see and self-correct typed refusals (UNRESOLVED, unsupported gate); argument-type errors are not distinguished (-32602).

JSON-RPC batches (arrays) and non-object messages fail with a parse error (id null); there is no request-size or time limit and no concurrency: tools run synchronously on the read loop, so one long SAT or simulation call blocks ping and cancellation.

The Studio HTTP API has no OpenAPI document, no public stable versioning for the non-QG routes (only /api/qg/v1 is versioned), no async job or SSE streaming, and by design no remote exposure or CORS; there is no hosted API, no remote MCP (Streamable HTTP) and no OAuth/auth for MCP.

No CLI/MCP/HTTP interface can submit to real hardware: this is deliberate (fail-closed) but means no provider job lifecycle (submit/status/result/cancel) and no qBraid/Qiskit Runtime/Braket-style adapters.

`hcs.run.v2` has a JSON Schema only for provenance cards; CLI JSON uses a separate `schema_version: "1.0"` (cli.py:49) with no published schema file, and MCP/Studio responses have no published schemas (no schemas/ directory).
defects_or_risks: MCP `cqhecs_sat_solve`/`sat_count`/`sat_models` take `timeout` with no upper bound (mcp_server.py:230,235,254,365,275), whereas Studio clamps to 0.01-30 s (studio/app.py:656); a prompt-injected or careless agent can pin the single-threaded server for arbitrary time. `shots` maximum 20000 is declared only in the schema; it is enforced just because _tool_run delegates to StudioState.simulate (app.py:416). `workers`, `waves` and `limit` are unbounded in the MCP omniwave and models paths.

MCP `cqhecs_run` builds a new `StudioState(ROOT)` on every call (mcp_server.py:177-179), which reloads datasets and profiles each time; this is a latency/consistency cost and couples MCP to Studio internals instead of a shared service layer.

Input-convention drift: CLI accepts `name:ghz8` while MCP analyze/plan/run accept only `preset:<name>` or raw QASM (mcp_server.py:197,211); and `plan` is exposed in MCP/Studio but has no dedicated CLI subcommand (only embedded in analyze, cli.py:918), which weakens the T6-01 'one schema' parity claim.

sota.takeaway: Standard for multi-platform wheels incl. Windows, with test-command and repair-wheel-command hooks; runs abi3audit automatically on abi3 wheels.

mutmut is Unix/WSL only (per search summary of a March 2026 comparison); project runs on Windows 11, so mutmut may not run natively. cosmic-ray is cross-platform but needs session DB.
An academic comparison snippet reported low competency for cosmic-ray and inconclusive results for mutmut; treat tool scores as tool-specific, not ground truth.

Comparator relies on landrun (Linux sandbox; needs main branch, has a stated vulnerability fixed in Linux 7.1), so running it on Windows needs WSL/CI Linux; fake-landrun.sh does no sandboxing and must not be used on untrusted input.

Licences not verified for any tool (cake_lpr, Comparator, Hypothesis MPL-2.0 recalled from memory only, HypoFuzz has a commercial/dual-licence angle I did not verify). Do not vendor code before checking.
